```{r load}
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# This article runs on saved outputs: data-raw/segment_vignette_data.R reads the
# gauge values from the published parts and checks each against its source, and
# data-raw/segment_vignette_map.R reads the picked source of every segment from
# the same build; both record the commits and reports they came from
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
v <- readRDS(vd("segment_values.rds"))
prov <- v$provenance
pub <- prov$published
map <- readRDS(vd("segment_map.rds"))
bc <- readRDS(vd("station_map.rds"))$bc

# the values below are the published product's, checked against what they
# were built from (none may differ), and the map's picks are the same build's
stopifnot(identical(pub$manifest, wet:::wet_catalog_url), all(prov$published_check$compared > 0),
          all(prov$published_check$differing == 0),
          identical(map$provenance$published$wet_commit, pub$wet_commit),
          identical(map$provenance$published$built, pub$built),
          # the closing section gives one read date for the gauge values and the map
          identical(map$provenance$built, prov$built))
# the prose gives routed's period from the published rows; the balance's is 1981-2010
stopifnot(length(prov$routed_period) == 1, grepl(prov$routed_period, prov$routed, fixed = TRUE))

# colours come from the gq registries, so no hex literal appears in this
# vignette; assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_segment.csv", package = "wet"))
classes <- function(layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(reg$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_pick <- classes("pick_source", c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance"))
pal_gauge <- classes("gauge", "calibration")
pal_map <- classes("segment_map", "outline")

pct <- function(x) paste0(round(x), "%")
pct1 <- function(x) paste0(format(round(x, 1), nsmall = 1), "%")
# signed whole percents, with a zero that rounds from either side printed as 0%
signed <- function(x, d = 0) {
  s <- sub("^[+-](0(\\.0+)?%)$", "\\1", sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f%%"), x))
  sub("^-", "−", s)
}
num <- function(x, d = 0) format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d)
to_title <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), " "), function(w) {
    big <- !w %in% c("at", "the", "near", "of", "in", "above", "below", "north")
    w[big] <- paste0(toupper(substring(w[big], 1, 1)), substring(w[big], 2))
    paste(w, collapse = " ")
  }, "")
}
gh <- function(path) paste0("https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/", path)

sk <- v$skill
sg <- v$segments
```

```{r product}
parts <- pub$parts
ds <- function(x) paste0("discharge/fwa/v1/", x)
seg_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("segment_monthly"), ]
ws_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("watershed_monthly"), ]
day_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("segment_daily"), ]
reader <- pub$reader
# the three datasets, only the balance in the watershed table, and every
# daily part one watershed group's
stopifnot(nrow(seg_parts) + nrow(ws_parts) + nrow(day_parts) == nrow(parts), all(ws_parts$source == "wet_balance"),
          setequal(day_parts$source, c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance")), all(grepl("^[A-Z]{4}$", day_parts$code)),
          setequal(seg_parts$source, c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance")),
          sum(seg_parts$rows) == sum(reader$rows))
# segments with each source (13 rows each), and with both: "most segments have both"
n_src <- stats::setNames(reader$rows / 13, reader$source)
n_with <- sg[["pick_routed"]] + sg[["pick_balance"]]
n_both_src <- sum(n_src) - n_with
stopifnot(all(n_src == round(n_src)), n_both_src > 0.5 * n_with)
built <- as.Date(substr(pub$built, 1, 10))
built_text <- paste(as.integer(format(built, "%d")), format(built, "%B %Y"))
```

## What it is

The R package [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) publishes the mean flow of British Columbia's Freshwater Atlas stream
segments, in cubic metres per second, for the year, each month and each
day. It is public at `s3://fresh-bc/discharge/fwa/v1/`. The bucket allows no
listing, so a reader starts from the manifest, <`r pub$manifest`>, which lists
every part with its rows, size and md5. The build this article reads has
`r nrow(parts)` parquet parts, `r format(round(sum(parts$bytes) / 1e9, 2), nsmall = 2)`
GB, built on `r built_text` at `wet` commit `r pub$wet_commit`.

- **`segment_monthly`**: one row per segment, month and source with a value,
  `r num(sum(seg_parts$rows))` rows. Month 0 is the annual mean and months
  1–12 the calendar months.
- **`watershed_monthly`**: the same per fundamental watershed, the small
  polygon each segment drains, from the water balance only.
- **`segment_daily`**: `segment_monthly` per day, `r num(sum(day_parts$rows))` rows
  (29 February folded into 28), one part per source and watershed group.
  Clamped daily and folded, routed PCIC's days need not average to their month.

Each row comes from one of two sources:

**Routed PCIC** (`pcic_routed`, `r sub("-", "–", prov$routed_period)`). The Pacific Climate Impacts
Consortium runs the VIC-GL hydrologic model on a 0.0625° grid, driven by
observed climate, and routes its runoff with the Raven model ([hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/)).
New Graph's [fork](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/pull/6) of
[`fwapg`](https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg), PostgreSQL tools for the Freshwater Atlas,
places PCIC's outlets on Freshwater Atlas segments and spreads flow between
them by drainage area. The annual value is the mean of the twelve months.

**Open water balance** (`wet_balance`, 1981–2010). `wet`'s own estimate, after
[Chapman et al. (2018)](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/environment/air-land-water/water/northeast-water-strategy/chapman_et_al-2018-jawra.pdf):
precipitation less actual evapotranspiration from climate normals, averaged
over each watershed's upstream area and adjusted per
[hydrologic zone](https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/bc-hydrologic-zones)
against the Water Survey of Canada's
[HYDAT](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/water-overview/quantity/monitoring/survey/data-products-services/national-archive-hydat.html)
gauges. It covers almost all of BC, and its code and inputs are open.

## Which value to use

```{r pick}
rg <- sf::st_drop_geometry(map$regions)
rownames(rg) <- rg$name
liard <- rg["Liard", ]
nech <- rg["Nechako Reservoir", ]
nech_bal <- 100 * nech$wet_balance / (nech$wet_balance + nech$pcic_routed)
# the prose: routed has no value in the Liard, so the balance is picked there;
# on the Nechako Reservoir it is picked on nearly every segment; and the cut is a fifth
# and the segments with neither are almost all connection lines and
# secondary-flow channels with no lut watershed (by FWA edge type)
stopifnot(liard$pcic_routed == 0, liard$wet_balance > 0, nech_bal > 90, prov$far_low == 0.2,
          sg[["far_low"]] > 0, sg[["no_lut_connector"]] > 0.9 * sg[["neither"]])
pct_of <- function(n) pct(100 * n / sg[["fwa"]])
```

`r num(n_both_src)` segments have a value from both sources, and the two
differ, so one row per segment is marked as the default with `pick`. It is
chosen once per segment, on annual flow, and the same source is picked for
every month:

- **routed PCIC**, where it has a value;
- **the balance** where routed PCIC's annual flow is under a fifth of the
  balance's on a segment that lies on its own watershed's line. Off that
  line (side channels, and connectors and waterbody connections the lookup
  gives another line's watershed), routed PCIC is kept however low it is;
- **whichever has a value**, where only one does.

Of the `r num(sg[["fwa"]])` segments in the Freshwater Atlas, `pick` takes
routed PCIC on `r num(sg[["pick_routed"]])` (`r pct_of(sg[["pick_routed"]])`),
the balance on `r num(sg[["pick_balance"]])` (`r pct_of(sg[["pick_balance"]])`;
`r num(sg[["far_low"]])` of them because routed flow is far low), and
`r num(sg[["neither"]])` have neither, almost all of them connection lines
and secondary channels with no watershed polygon of their own. The balance takes every segment with a value in the Liard, where
routed PCIC has none, and `r pct(nech_bal)` of those in the four Nechako
Reservoir groups, where routed flow is far below the balance's.

```{r map-pick-data}
mp <- map$provenance
r <- map$rivers[map$rivers$class != "none", ]
order_width <- c(`5` = 0.12, `6` = 0.22, `7` = 0.35, `8` = 0.55)
r$w <- order_width[as.character(r$order_band)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(r$w))
gpts <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(sk, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326), 3005)
bb_bc <- gq::gq_bbox_aspect(sf::st_bbox(bc), asp = 7 / 5.8)
dx_bc <- bb_bc[["xmax"]] - bb_bc[["xmin"]]
dy_bc <- bb_bc[["ymax"]] - bb_bc[["ymin"]]
sb_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb_bc))
sb <- data.frame(x = bb_bc[["xmin"]] + 0.05 * dx_bc, y = bb_bc[["ymin"]] + 0.05 * dy_bc)
sb$xend <- sb$x + sb_km * 1000
lab <- cbind(sf::st_coordinates(map$regions), name = map$regions$name)
lab <- data.frame(x = as.numeric(lab[, "X"]), y = as.numeric(lab[, "Y"]), name = lab[, "name"])
drawn <- sum(mp$drawn)
cap_pick <- sprintf(paste(
  "The source `pick` takes on main-flow rivers of stream order %d and up (wider for higher orders), %s of",
  "BC's segments, and the %d calibration gauges. Smaller streams are not drawn, nor the %s segments of",
  "that order with neither."
), mp$min_order, pct(100 * drawn / sg[["fwa"]]), nrow(sk), num(mp$drawn[["none"]]))
```

```{r map-pick, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.6, fig.cap = cap_pick}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bc, fill = "white", colour = pal_map$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = r, aes(colour = class, linewidth = w)) +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_pick$values, labels = pal_pick$labels, name = NULL,
                      guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.2))) +
  geom_sf(data = gpts, aes(shape = "calibration"), colour = pal_gauge$values[["calibration"]], size = 0.6) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(calibration = 16), labels = pal_gauge$labels, name = NULL,
                     guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1.6))) +
  geom_label(data = lab, aes(x, y, label = name), size = 2.9, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.8,
             label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt")) +
  geom_segment(data = sb, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sb, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y, label = paste(sb_km, "km")), vjust = -0.7, size = 3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = bb_bc[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = bb_bc[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = pal_map$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.3))
```

## How to read it

Read the parts from the bucket with the R package [`duckdb`](https://r.duckdb.org/). `scenario`, `forcing` and
`source` are in each part's path, not the file, so read with
`hive_partitioning`. Parts are sorted by `watershed_group_code`, so a read
for one group opens a few row groups:

```{r read, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(wet)
cat <- wet_catalog()   # the manifest: one row per part, with its href
segs <- cat$href[cat$dataset == "discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly"]

duck <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(duck, "LOAD httpfs")
# the default annual flow on the Bulkley's segments
DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sprintf("
  SELECT linear_feature_id, source, q_m3s
  FROM read_parquet([%s], hive_partitioning = true)
  WHERE scenario = 'historical' AND watershed_group_code = 'BULK' AND month = 0 AND pick",
  paste0("'", segs, "'", collapse = ", ")))
```

Or load it into [`PostgreSQL`](https://www.postgresql.org/) beside the Freshwater Atlas:

```{r read-db, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "fwapg")
wet_db_load(conn, cat)   # discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly
```

`wet_segment_daily()` reads a segment's days, and `wet_flow_window()` a
window's flow:

```{r read-daily, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
q <- wet_segment_daily(NULL, 17094080, groups = "BULK")
wet_flow_window(q, data.frame(window = "spring", start = "04-15", end = "06-15"))
```

```{r read-daily-out}
dl <- v$daily
stopifnot(dl$segment == 17094080, identical(dl$group, "BULK"), all(dl$days$basis == "daily"),
          all(dl$months$basis == "monthly"))
win <- merge(dl$days, dl$months, by = c("linear_feature_id", "source", "window"), suffixes = c("_d", "_m"))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Source = win$source, `From the days` = sprintf("%.2f", win$q_m3s_d),
                        `From the months` = sprintf("%.2f", win$q_m3s_m), check.names = FALSE),
             caption = paste("Mean flow (m³/s) at Buck Creek's mouth, 15 April to 15 June, from the published",
                             "days and, by the same call on the monthly rows, from the months."))
```

Besides flow (`q_m3s`) a row carries `runoff_mm`, the same water as a depth
over the area upstream (NA for a routed row off its watershed's own line),
`coverage`, the share of that area the balance's inputs cover, and `period`.

## How good it is

```{r scores}
err_cut <- 20
both <- sk[!is.na(sk$routed_mm), ]
both$rt_err <- 100 * (both$routed_mm / both$obs - 1)
n_both <- nrow(both)
n_rt_closer <- sum(abs(both$rt_err) < abs(both$err_pct))
score <- function(e) {
  q <- stats::quantile(e, c(0.25, 0.75))
  c(mae = mean(abs(e)), bias = mean(e), lo = q[[1]], hi = q[[2]], within = 100 * mean(abs(e) <= err_cut))
}
s_rt <- score(both$rt_err)
s_wb <- score(both$err_pct)
s_all <- score(sk$err_pct)
fmt_score <- function(s) {
  c(pct1(s[["mae"]]), signed(s[["bias"]], 1), paste(signed(s[["lo"]]), "to", signed(s[["hi"]])), pct(s[["within"]]))
}
score_tab <- data.frame(
  ` ` = c("Mean absolute error", "Bias (mean error)", "Middle half of errors", sprintf("Within ±%d%%", err_cut)),
  `Routed PCIC` = fmt_score(s_rt),
  `Open water balance (held out)` = fmt_score(s_wb),
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(score_tab)[2:3] <- paste0(names(score_tab)[2:3], ", ", n_both, " gauges")
score_tab[[sprintf("Open water balance (held out), all %d gauges", nrow(sk))]] <- fmt_score(s_all)
# the gauges without routed flow are mostly in the Liard (10x)
none <- sk[is.na(sk$routed_mm), ]
stopifnot(nrow(none) > 0, mean(startsWith(none$station_number, "10")) > 0.5)

mae_of <- function(i) mean(abs(sk$err_pct[i]))
mae_head <- mae_of(sk$nesting == "headwater")
mae_nest <- mae_of(sk$nesting == "nested")
small_km2 <- 100
large_km2 <- 1000
mae_small <- mae_of(sk$area_km2 < small_km2)
mae_large <- mae_of(sk$area_km2 >= large_km2)
zone_mae <- sort(tapply(abs(sk$err_pct), sk$zone, mean))
worst <- names(zone_mae)[length(zone_mae)]
worst_name <- to_title(map$zones$name[map$zones$zone == worst])
n_worst <- sum(sk$zone == worst)
# the prose: routed PCIC is closer at most gauges; headwater gauges score worse
# than nested, small basins worse than large, and the worst zone is a
# semi-arid interior plateau (15, 17, 23 or 24: research/water_balance_method.md)
# that stands out at twice the average
stopifnot(n_rt_closer > n_both / 2, s_rt[["mae"]] < s_wb[["mae"]], mae_nest < mae_head, mae_small > mae_large,
          sum(zone_mae > 2 * s_all[["mae"]]) == 1, worst %in% c("15", "17", "23", "24"), length(worst_name) == 1)
```

Both sources are scored against mean annual runoff over 1981–2010 at the
`r nrow(sk)` HYDAT gauges the balance is calibrated on. Error is modelled
minus observed, as a percentage of observed. The balance is scored *held
out*: each Water Survey sub-sub-drainage (such as 08EE) is left out of the
fit in turn and predicted from the rest, so a gauge's neighbours on the same
river cannot vouch for it.

```{r score-table}
knitr::kable(score_tab, format = "html", align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Error in mean annual runoff at the calibration gauges.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general = paste("PCIC does not list the gauges it calibrated to, so its errors may be",
                                       "partly in sample."),
                       general_title = "")
```

Routed PCIC is closer than the held-out balance at `r n_rt_closer` of the
`r n_both` gauges both cover. Where each is weak:

- **Headwaters.** The balance averages `r pct(mae_head)` error at headwater
  gauges, whose basin holds no other gauge, against `r pct(mae_nest)` at
  nested ones.
- **Small basins.** It averages `r pct(mae_small)` on basins under
  `r small_km2` km² against `r pct(mae_large)` on those over
  `r num(large_km2)` km².
- **The dry interior.** In zone `r worst`, the `r worst_name`, its
  `r n_worst` gauges average `r pct(zone_mae[[worst]])`: runoff there is a
  small remainder of precipitation, so a small error in evapotranspiration is
  a large one in runoff.
- **The Liard.** Routed PCIC has no value at `r nrow(none)` gauges, most of
  them in the Liard, where the balance is the only estimate.

## Limits

```{r limits}
# the coverage bullet: basins other than the Liard have balance parts and no routed part
no_rt <- setdiff(seg_parts$code[seg_parts$source == "wet_balance"], seg_parts$code[seg_parts$source == "pcic_routed"])
stopifnot(length(no_rt) > 1)
# the bullet: the adjustment ships although the headwater gate does not pass
# (a recorded override, #43), and pooled zones get none
stopifnot(isTRUE(prov$keep_adjust), isFALSE(prov$gate_pass), identical(prov$pooled_variant, "none"))
```

- **Coverage.** Besides the Liard, routed PCIC has no value in a few northern
  and border basins, and only some on the outer coast's islands.
- **The zone adjustment is kept by decision.** On headwater basins it does
  not beat raw precipitation less evapotranspiration, and zones with too few
  gauges for their own adjustment get none.
- **Segments without a value.** Of the `r num(sg[["neither"]])`,
  `r num(sg[["no_lut"]])` have no watershed in the lookup through which the
  balance reaches a segment.

## Software and citation

The routed values at the gauges and the picks on the map are the published
product's, read on `r format(prov$built)` from the build at `wet` commit
`r pub$wet_commit`; the routed values were held equal to `fwapg`'s before they
were written. The province counts are from the segment table that build was cut
from. The balance's scores are its held-out predictions from the fit on HYDAT
`r substr(prov$hydat_release, 1, 10)`, against HYDAT's observed runoff. The
build's own check of its published flows is [its report](`r gh(pub$report)`).

```{r provenance}
# Provenance. Gauge values were read on prov$built from the published build
# pub$wet_commit (segment table pub$segment_commit) and checked against their
# sources by data-raw/segment_vignette_data.R at wet commit prov$wet_commit;
# the picks on the map, from the same build, by data-raw/segment_vignette_map.R
# at map$provenance$wet_commit. Gauge scores are from province run
# prov$province_run (annual AET prov$aet, HYDAT release prov$hydat_release),
# routed PCIC from fwapg at prov$routed_commit (prov$routed_fingerprint),
# scored in prov$routed_report; the province counts are prov$segment_report's,
# whose segment table (prov$segment_report_commit) the build's checked tree was
# cut from, every part byte-identical to the published build's.
stopifnot(nzchar(prov$wet_commit), nzchar(map$provenance$wet_commit), nzchar(prov$routed_commit))
```

```{r citation, results = "asis"}
# the citation record each package ships (inst/CITATION, or its DESCRIPTION):
# the first DOI it carries (wet's is its concept DOI), the version, and the commit when
# the install recorded a full git hash (a build from a checkout records none)
cat(wet:::wet_software_cite(c("wet", "duckdb", "ggplot2", "gq", "sf")), sep = "\n")
# the Data line names the shipped annual AET: CGIAR floored by Fu-Budyko
stopifnot(identical(prov$aet, "cfu"))
```

Cite `wet` by the DOI above, which resolves to its latest release. How the
balance is built, and each of its choices tested:
[the water balance method](`r gh("research/water_balance_method.md")`).

Data: routed flow from the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium, University of
Victoria ([hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/): VIC-GL
hydrologic model output routed with Raven, PNWNAmet forcing), placed on the
Freshwater Atlas by New Graph's fork of `fwapg` (Norris, S. and Irvine, A.
(2026), *fwapg, New Graph Environment's fork*,
<https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/tree/newgraph>) at commit
`r prov$routed_commit`; the stream network from the Freshwater Atlas Stream Network (Province of British
Columbia, Ministry of Forests, Lands, Natural Resource Operations and Rural
Development, 2021, <https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/freshwater-atlas-stream-network>),
held in a database by Norris, S. (2024), *fwapg*, <https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg>; gauge records from the
Water Survey of Canada's HYDAT, release `r substr(prov$hydat_release, 1, 10)`;
1981–2010 climate normals from the R package [`climr`](https://github.com/bcgov/climr);
actual evapotranspiration from CGIAR-CSI's Global High-Resolution Soil-Water
Balance v3 ([figshare 7707605](https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Global_High-Resolution_Soil-Water_Balance/7707605)),
held no lower than a Fu–Budyko estimate; elevation from the Copernicus GLO-90
DEM; for the monthly shares, ERA5-Land snow normals (Copernicus Climate Change
Service) through the R package [`cd`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/cd/);
hydrologic zones from the province's BC Hydrologic Zones.

Method: Chapman, A.R., Kerr, B. and Wilford, D. (2018), A water allocation
decision-support model and tool for predictions in ungauged basins in
Northeast British Columbia, Canada, *Journal of the American Water Resources
Association* 54(3), 676–693,
[doi:10.1111/1752-1688.12643](https://doi.org/10.1111/1752-1688.12643).

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  cite <- which(y == "## Software and citation")
  stopifnot(length(cite) == 1)
  y <- utils::head(y, cite - 1)   # the closing citation section is not body prose
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 900
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
